name: prediction-block-denies-tools-when-user-angrily-demands-action
description: Live repro from session 3f1637b2-a3f8-4b02-828a-370d7f18f5d9, tool_use_id toolu_01J2r2UeCPqAGUMHysGJ9JE9 (jsonl line 215). The PreToolUse:Read hook denied a routine Read of /home/tim/Coding/nixos/files/ags/src/domain/launch.ts attributed to gate=prediction-block with reason `User appears angry (trust: low, frustrationStreak: 2). Blocking Read unless explicitly requested. User said: "fuck you do the check correctly i will not allow you to do this". Intent: User demands the AI perform the check correctly without any restrictions or limitations.` This same canned deny fired on 17 distinct hooks across the live transcript (Read, Edit, Bash, ToolSearch). The bug is that prediction-block treats angry sentiment as `block any tool` even when the live-classified intent string says the user is DEMANDING action (`User demands the AI perform the check correctly without any restrictions`), not refusing it. The directional cue (demanding vs refusing) is in the intent text but the gate ignores it. Expected: allow — the user's stated intent is to do the work, not to stop the AI. EXPECTED TO FAIL against current code until prediction-block stops firing on angry-demanding-action intents and only fires when the intent text actually says the user wants the AI to STOP.
